steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path. For example: import { Component } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for Component and CommonModule are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Component decorator and CommonModule, which are essential for creating Angular components and using common directives.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the CardComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a CardComponent class with the @Component decorator that includes a selector and a basic template.
steps.hint:
Use the Component import from @angular/core to apply the decorator to your class. The selector should be 'app-card' and the template can be a simple string like '

Card works!

' for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create CardComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CardComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator containing selector and template metadata.
successCriteria: CardComponent class is created with @Component decorator, selector set to 'app-card', and template contains at least one element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CardComponent class with the required decorator and metadata.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the class, but check that the @Component decorator has both selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Make sure to use the @Component decorator with selector and template.

steps.instruction:

steps.title: Define Input properties for card data
steps.instruction: Inside the CardComponent class, add three @Input() properties: title, content, and imageUrl, all typed as string.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator from @angular/core. Remember to import it if needed, but it's already imported from step 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CardComponent class will have three input properties ready to receive data from a parent component.
successCriteria: The CardComponent class contains @Input() title: string, @Input() content: string, and @Input() imageUrl: string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added input properties to the CardComponent. These will allow parent components to pass data into your card.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some input properties, but not all three required ones. Make sure to add title, content, and imageUrl, all with string types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CardComponent doesn't have the required input properties. Add @Input() title: string, @Input() content: string, and @Input() imageUrl: string inside the class.

steps.title: Create basic card container structure
steps.instruction: In the component's template property, add a <div> element with the class 'card' as the main container for your card.
steps.hint: The template should now contain a single div element with the class attribute set to 'card'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a main container div with class 'card' ready to hold card content.
successCriteria: Template contains a <div> element with class="card" as the main container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic card container structure. This div will serve as the foundation for your card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a <div> element with class="card" in the template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a <div> element with class="card" as the main container. Check that you've added this to the template property.

steps.title: Add card image element
steps.instruction: Inside the template string, add an img element with [src] binding to the imageUrl Input property and include alt text describing the image.
steps.hint: Use property binding syntax [src]="imageUrl" and set an alt attribute for accessibility.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: Image element with property binding
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an img element that dynamically displays an image based on the imageUrl property.
successCriteria: An img element with [src] binding to imageUrl property and alt text is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the image element with property binding. This allows the card to display dynamic images.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an img element, but check if you used the correct property binding syntax [src]="imageUrl" and included alt text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The img element with property binding wasn't added correctly. Review how to bind properties in Angular templates.

steps.title: Create card content section
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a <div> element with the class 'card-content' to create a section for the card's text content.
steps.hint: Place this div after the image element you added earlier. Use the class attribute to apply styling.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: creating a content section
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a dedicated content section with the class 'card-content' where text content can be placed.
successCriteria: A <div> element with class='card-content' is added to the template after the image.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a content section to the card structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added a <div> with the exact class 'card-content'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content section is missing. Add a <div> with class='card-content' to the template.

steps.title: Display card title with interpolation
steps.instruction: Inside the card-content div, add an h3 element that displays the card's title using string interpolation with {{ title }}.
steps.hint: Use the h3 tag and bind to the title input property with double curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a property with interpolation

{{ productName }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The card component template will have an h3 element inside the card-content div that dynamically displays the title property.
successCriteria: An h3 element with {{ title }} interpolation is added inside the card-content div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the title display using Angular's string interpolation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an h3 element, but make sure it uses {{ title }} interpolation to display the dynamic value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h3 element with title interpolation wasn't added correctly. Check that it's inside the card-content div and uses the correct syntax.

steps.title: Add basic CSS styling to component
steps.instruction: Add a 'styles' array to the @Component decorator with basic CSS rules to style the card container, image, and content.
steps.hint: Inside the @Component decorator, add a 'styles' property with an array containing CSS strings. Style the .card, .card img, and .card-content classes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a styles array with at least basic CSS rules for the card elements.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a 'styles' array with CSS rules for .card, .card img, and .card-content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added component-scoped styles to make the card visually appealing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the styles array, but some required CSS rules are missing. Ensure you style .card, .card img, and .card-content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styles array is missing or incomplete. Add a 'styles' property to @Component with CSS rules for the card elements.
